class.name: NetwLagCompensationConfig
class.brief_description: How long the server waits for a late player action, and how far ahead of itself it will take one.
class.description: Two numbers, both optional. [method Netw.configure_lagcomp] returns one of these to fill in. [codeblock] func _init() -> void: Netw.configure_lagcomp(self) \ .input_gate_deadline_ticks(16) \ .max_future_action_ticks(4) [/codeblock] Declaring this does not turn lag compensation on. The recording starts itself as soon as a predicted node or a [NetwAction] needs it, so a game that predicts declares nothing here and a game that predicts nothing pays for nothing. Declare one to move a number off its default. Once the session has read these values they are its own, so freeing the node that declared them stops nothing, and there is no way to take them back. A value written afterwards is reported and changes nothing.

method.name: input_gate_deadline_ticks
method.description: Sets [member input_gate_deadline_ticks] and returns this same config, so a declaration reads as one chained expression.

method.name: max_future_action_ticks
method.description: Sets [member max_future_action_ticks] and returns this same config, so a declaration reads as one chained expression.

members.member: How many ticks a [constant NetwAction.TIMING_TICK_ALIGNED_STATE_READY] action waits for the state its tick needs before it gives up and resolves on what it has. Raise it for a link that loses input often, and lower it to return a player sooner at the cost of judging on less. A negative count is rejected and the previous value stands.

How far ahead of the server's own tick an action may ask to happen before it is denied. This is what stops a client claiming it acted in the future. A negative count is rejected and the previous value stands.
